land.text: Asia Minor, where Achaeus 'assumed the title of king'

predecessors.note: The page says 'Asia Minor' in 220 and 'western Anatolia' in 216; the region is the Seleucid land of the 218 shape in Lydia, Phrygia, Ionia and Caria.

land.text: Sardis, whose citadel 'managed to hold out until 213 BC'

capitals.name: Sardis
capitals.note: The page names Sardis only as Achaeus's last refuge ('driven him from the field into Sardis' by 214; the citadel held until 213). Earlier seat not named on the page; coordinates are the ruins of Sardis.

correction.text: western Asia Minor (Lydia, Phrygia, Ionia, Caria) held by Achaeus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Achaeus 'assumed the title of king in Asia Minor' in 220; the page defines no frontier, so the land is the Seleucid part of Lydia, Phrygia, Ionia and Caria in the 218 shape (161 cells). Antiochus III returned to Syria, and the page gives no event until the 216 expedition.

correction.text: Sardis and its surroundings, where Achaeus was driven by 214

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: by 214 Antiochus 'had by 214 BC driven him from the field into Sardis'; the citadel 'managed to hold out until 213 BC' under Achaeus's widow.

ledger.note: 220: Achaeus declares himself king in Asia Minor. He 'assumed the title of king in Asia Minor' while Antiochus III turned back to Syria. The page gives the region, not its extent.
216: Antiochus marches against Achaeus. 'In 216 BC his army marched into western Anatolia to suppress the local rebellion'.
214: Achaeus is driven into Sardis. He was driven 'from the field into Sardis' by 214; the open country returns to the king.
213: the siege of Sardis ends. The citadel 'managed to hold out until 213 BC'; the page gives no year for Achaeus's capture and execution.
213: Achaeus's last land falls to Antiochus III.
213: the kingdom of Achaeus ends when the citadel of Sardis falls.

wars.name: Revolt of Achaeus
wars.outcome: Antiochus III marches in 216, drives Achaeus into Sardis by 214 and takes the citadel in 213.

certainty.note: No frontier of the rebel kingdom is described; the land is the Seleucid west as Cliopatria draws it.

notes: Rebel state added by me-05-c. One page (Antiochus III the Great) names the revolt; it gives 220 for the royal title, 216 for the campaign, 214 for the retreat into Sardis and 213 for the citadel. Not on the page: Achaeus's earlier seat, his alliance, his death. The Seleucid Empire dossier carries the matching loss (220) and gain (213).
